extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (computational algebraists, commutative algebra researchers) seeking API documentation for library procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in SINGULAR libraries (monomialideal.lib, mprimdec.lib, mregular.lib, noether.lib), stating usage, return values, assumptions, notes, and examples for each procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: minbaseMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minbaseMon (I); I ideal. Return: an ideal, the minimal monomial generators of I. (-1 if the generators of I are not monomials). Assume: I is an ideal generated by a list of monomials of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Procedure from monomialideal.lib. Example shown using LIB "monomialideal.lib"; ring R = 0,(w,x,y,z,t),lp; ideal I = ...; minbaseMon(I); returns the minimal monomial generators (e.g. w3xy, y3z, wxyzt, x2z4t3, x2y2z2).

rubrics_metrics.name: gcdMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gcdMon (f,g); f,g polynomials. Return: a monomial, the greatest common divisor of f and g. Assume: f and g are monomials of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From monomialideal.lib. Example: gcdMon(x^3*z^5*t^2, y^6*z^3*t^3) -> z3t2.

rubrics_metrics.name: lcmMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lcmMon (f,g); f,g polynomials. Return: a monomial, the least common multiple of f and g. Assume: f,g are monomials of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: lcmMon(x^3*z^5*t^2, y^6*z^3*t^3) -> x3y6z5t3.

rubrics_metrics.name: membershipMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: membershipMon(f,I); f polynomial, I ideal. Return: 1 if f lies in I; 0 otherwise. (-1 if I and f are nonzero and I is not a monomial ideal). Assume: I is a monomial ideal of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: membershipMon applied to particular polynomials/ideals returns 1 or 0. From monomialideal.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: intersectMon (I,J); I,J ideals. Return: an ideal, the intersection of I and J. (returns -1 if I or J are not monomial ideals). Assume: I,J are monomial ideals of the basering. Note: the minimal monomial generating set is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows intersection of two ideals returning a minimal monomial generating set (list of monomials).

rubrics_metrics.name: quotientMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: quotientMon (I,J); I,J ideals. Return: an ideal, the quotient I:J. (returns -1 if I or J is not monomial). Assume: I,J are monomial ideals of the basering. Note: the minimal monomial generating set is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates quotientMon producing a list of generators for I:J.

rubrics_metrics.name: radicalMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: radicalMon(I); I ideal. Return: an ideal, the radical ideal of the ideal I. (returns -1 if I is not a monomial ideal). Assume: I is a monomial ideal of the basering. Note: the minimal monomial generating set is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: radicalMon returns generators like yz, xzt, wxy for a given ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: isprimeMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isprimeMon (I); I ideal. Return: 1, if I is prime; 0, otherwise. (returns -1 if I is not a monomial ideal). Assume: I is a monomial ideal of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: isprimeMon(w,y,t) -> 1; isprimeMon(w,y,t,x*z) -> 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: isprimaryMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isprimaryMon (I); I ideal. Return: 1, if I is primary; 0, otherwise. (returns -1 if I is not a monomial ideal). Assume: I is a monomial ideal of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show testing ideals that are primary or not; from monomialideal.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: isirreducibleMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isirreducibleMon(I); I ideal. Return: 1, if I is irreducible; 0, otherwise. (return -1 if I is not a monomial ideal). Assume: I is a monomial ideal of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: isirreducibleMon for w^4,x^3,z^2,t^5 returns 1; adding another generator can change to 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: isartinianMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isartinianMon(I); I ideal. Return: 1, if ideal is artinian; 0, otherwise. (return -1 if ideal I is not a monmial ideal). Assume: I is a monomial ideal of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate usage and return 1 or 0 depending on whether ideal is artinian.

rubrics_metrics.name: isgenericMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isgenericMon(I); I ideal. Return: 1, if ideal is generic; 0, otherwise. (return -1 if ideal I is not a monomial ideal). Assume: I is a monomial ideal of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show detection of generic vs non-generic ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: dimMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dimMon (I); I ideal. Return: an integer, the dimension of the affine variety defined by the ideal I. (returns -1 if I is not a monomial ideal). Assume: I is a monomial ideal of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: dimMon returns dimension values (e.g. 3, 0) for given ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: irreddecMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: irreddecMon (I[,alg]); I ideal, alg string. Return: list, the irreducible components of the monomial ideal I. (returns -1 if I is not a monomial ideal). Assume: I is a monomial ideal of the basering k[x(1)..x(n)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Optional 'alg' selects algorithm: 'vas' (Vasconcelos direct), 'add' (Alexander dual + double dual), 'ad' (Alexander dual + quotients), 'for' (formula), 'mil' (Scarf complex), 'lr' (Roune label), 'gz' (Gao-Zhu), 'sr' (Roune slice). Examples show outputs for different algorithms and list forms of components.

rubrics_metrics.name: primdecMon
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primdecMon (I[,alg]); I ideal, alg string. Return: list, the components in a minimal primary decomposition of I. (returns -1 if I is not a monomial ideal). Assume: I is a monomial ideal of the basering k[x(1)..x(n)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Optional 'alg' selects various algorithms (vp, vi, add, ad, for, mil, lr, gz, sr) from irreducible decompositions and other conversions. Examples show minimal primary decompositions produced by different methods (Vasconcelos, Alexander dual, label algorithm, slice algorithm).

rubrics_metrics.name: separator
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: separator(l); list l of prime ideals. Return: a list of separators of the prime ideals in l, i.e. polynomials p_ij such that p_ij is in l[j] for all l[j] not contained in l[i] but p_ij is not in l[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example demonstrates separator(minAssGTZ(i)) returning polynomials like x and y for given primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimdecA
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PrimdecA (N[, i]); module N, int i. Return: list l a (not necessarily minimal) primary decomposition of N computed by a generalized version of the algorithm of Shimoyama/Yokoyama; if i!=0 is given, the factorizing Groebner is used to compute the isolated primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Examples show decomposition outputs as lists of submodules/ideals for a given module N.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimdecB
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: PrimdecB (N, p); pseudo-primary module N, isolated prime ideal p. Return: list l a (not necessarily minimal) primary decomposition of N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example: PrimdecB applied to a module and isolated prime returns component lists and generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: modDec
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modDec (N[, i]); module N, int i. Return: list l a minimal primary decomposition of N computed by a generalized version of the algorithm of Shimoyama/Yokoyama; if i=1 is given, the factorizing Groebner basis algorithm is used internally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Examples show modDec giving minimal decompositions and using factorizing Groebner when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: zeroMod
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: zeroMod (N[, check]); zero-dimensional module N[, module check]. Return: list l the minimal primary decomposition of a zero-dimensional module N, computed by a generalized version of the algorithm of Gianni, Trager and Zacharias. Note: if parameter check is given, only components not containing check are computed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example demonstrates decomposition of a module in one variable z with components corresponding to z, z+1, z-1 etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: GTZmod
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GTZmod (N[, check]); module N[, module check]. Return: list l the minimal primary decomposition of the module N, computed by a generalized version of the algorithm of Gianni, Trager and Zacharias. Note: if the parameter check is given, only components not containing check are computed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example shows GTZmod(N) producing minimal decomposition lists; similar behavior to zeroMod but generalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: dec1var
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dec1var (N); zero-dimensional module N. Return: list l the minimal primary decomposition of a submodule N of R^s if nvars(R)=1. Note: if parameter check is given, only components not containing check are computed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example decomposes a module over ring with one variable z returning components and associated generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: annil
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: annil(N); module N. Return: ideal ann = std(quotient(N,freemodule(nrows(N)))); the annihilator of M/N in the basering. Note: ann is a std basis in the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example: annil(x*gen(1), y*gen(2)) returns ann[1]=xy.

rubrics_metrics.name: splitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: splitting(N[,check[, ann]]); module N, module check, ideal ann. Return: (l, check) list l, module check. The elements of l consist of quadruples where [1] is module, [2],[3],[4] are ideals such that the intersection of the modules equals the zero-dimensional module N; l[j][3]=annil(l[j][1]) and l[j][4] contains internal ideal data; if l[j][2]!=0 then l[j][1] is primary with associated prime l[j][2], and check=intersect(check, l[j][1]) is computed. Note: if check given, only components not containing check are computed; if ann given, ann is used instead of annil(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example shows splitting on module N in ring z producing lists of module components and check module.

rubrics_metrics.name: primTest
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primTest(i[, p]); a zero-dimensional ideal i, irreducible poly p in i. Return: if i is neither prime nor homogeneous then ideal(0) is returned, otherwise radical(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Examples show primTest on ideals returning primes or radical ideals; used to test primality/homogeneity of zero-dimensional ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: preComp
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: preComp(N,check[, ann]); module N, module check, ideal ann. Return: (l, check) list l, module check. The elements of l consist of a triple with [1] module [2] and [3] ideals such that the intersection of the modules equals the zero-dimensional module N; l[j][3]=annil(l[j][1]) and if l[j][2]!=0 then l[j][1] is primary with associated prime l[j][2], and check=intersect(check, l[j][1]) is computed. Note: only components not containing check are computed; if ann is given, ann is used instead of annil(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example uses preComp on a module in one-variable ring and returns triples and check module.

rubrics_metrics.name: indSet
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: indSet(i); i ideal. Return: list with two entries: first gives strings for all maximal independent sets; second gives independent sets which cannot be enhanced. Each entry: lists of new varstrings with dependent variables, the independent set, the ordstring with corresponding block ordering, and integer where independent set starts in varstring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example demonstrates indSet on an ideal returning lists of variable groupings, block orderings, and positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: GTZopt
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GTZopt (N[, check]); module N[, module check]. Return: list l the minimal primary decomposition of the module N, computed by a generalized and optimized version of the algorithm of Gianni, Trager and Zacharias. Note: if check is given, only components not containing check are computed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example: GTZopt behaves like GTZmod but optimized; returns minimal decomposition lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: zeroOpt
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: zeroOpt (N[, check]); zero-dimensional module N[, module check]. Return: list l the minimal primary decomposition of a zero-dimensional module N, computed by a generalized and optimized version of the algorithm of Gianni, Trager and Zacharias. Note: if check given, only components not containing check are computed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mprimdec.lib. Example: zeroOpt returns component modules and corresponding generators for one-variable examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: regIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: regIdeal (i[,e]); i ideal, e integer. Return: an integer, the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of i. (returns -1 if i is not homogeneous). Assume: i is a homogeneous ideal of the basering S=K[x(0)..x(n)]. e=0 (default): if K infinite, makes random changes of coordinates; if K finite, works over transcendental extension. e=1: forces random changes even when K finite. It works if it terminates, but may loop; after 30 loops returns -1 with warning. If printlevel>0, additional info displayed (dim(S/i), depth(S/i), end(H^(depth(S/i))(S/i)), upper bound for a-invariant, whether regularity is attained at last step of minimal graded free resolution, regularity of Hilbert function if attained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mregular.lib. Example shows regIdeal applied to homogeneous ideal returning integer (e.g., 10) and an example of applying to lead(std(i)). Warning about possible infinite loop and printlevel for diagnostics.

rubrics_metrics.name: depthIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: depthIdeal (i[,e]); i ideal, e integer. Return: an integer, the depth of S/i where S=K[x(0)..x(n)] is the basering. (returns -1 if i is not homogeneous or if i=(1)). Assume: i is a proper homogeneous ideal. e parameter as in regIdeal: random changes of coordinates behavior; may loop; after 30 loops returns -1. Note: If printlevel>0, dim(S/i) is also displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mregular.lib. Example demonstrates depthIdeal(i) returns an integer (e.g., 1) and depth of lead(std(i)) possibly 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: satiety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: satiety (i[,e]); i ideal, e integer. Return: an integer, the satiety of i. (returns -1 if i is not homogeneous). Assume: i is a homogeneous ideal of the basering S=K[x(0)..x(n)]. e=0 default: satiety computed by determining fresh elements in socle; works over arbitrary fields. e=1: attempts random changes to find monomial ideal with same satiety; works over infinite fields; over finite fields may loop and after 30 loops returns -1. Theory: satiety is least s such that for all d>=s the degree d parts of i and sat(i,maxideal(1))[1] coincide. Note: If printlevel>0, dim(S/i) also displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From mregular.lib. Examples demonstrate satiety(i) returning integers (0 or 12), two methods (direct and coordinate change) and mention of method selection comments printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: regMonCurve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: regMonCurve (a0,...,an); ai integers with a0=0 < a1 < ... < an=:d. Return: an integer, the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the projective monomial curve C in P^n(K) parametrically defined by x(0)=t^d, x(1)=s^(a1)t^(d-a1), ..., x(n)=s^d where K=C. (returns -1 if a0=0<...<an is not satisfied). Assume: a0=0 < a1 < ... < an are integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: constructs defining ideal by elimination; uses regIdeal improvements exploiting monomial structure when ordering is dp and reg(C)=reg(lead(std(I))). If printlevel>0 extra diagnostics: whether C is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, end(H^1(S/I)), upper bound for a-invariant, step of minimal graded free resolution where regularity attained, regularity of Hilbert function. Examples include twisted cubic regMonCurve(0,1,2,3) -> 2 and another monomial curve -> 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: NoetherPosition
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NoetherPosition (i); i ideal. Return: a linear homogeneous transformation map phi = S,NoetherPosition(i); such that phi(i) is in Noether position, i.e., one has that K[x(n-d+1),...,x(n)] is a Noether normalization of S/phi(i) where S=K[x(0),...,x(n)] and d=dim(S/i). (returns -1 if i = (0) or (1)). Assume: The field K is infinite and i is a nonzero proper ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Works on finite fields if it terminates but may loop; after >30 loops returns -1 with warning. If printlevel>0 additional info (dim(S/i) and the Noether normalization variables) displayed. Examples show phi mapping variables to produce Noether position.

rubrics_metrics.name: is_NP
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is NP (i); i ideal. Return: 1 if K[x(n-d+1),...,x(n)] is a Noether normalization of S/i where S=K[x(0),...x(n)] and d=dim(S/i), 0 otherwise. (returns -1 if i=(0) or i=(1)). Assume: i is a nonzero proper homogeneous ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: If i is not homogeneous, is_NP(i)=1 can still indicate Noether normalization, but converse may fail. is_NP is used internally by regIdeal, depthIdeal, satiety, and NoetherPosition. Example shown returning 0 or 1 after mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: is_nested
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is nested (i); i monomial ideal. Return: 1 if i is of nested type, 0 otherwise. (returns -1 if i=(0) or i=(1)). Assume: i is a nonzero proper monomial ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: The ideal must be monomial; is_nested is used in depthIdeal, regIdeal and satiety. Definition: i is of nested type if its associated primes are all of the form (x(0),...,x(i)) for some i<=n. Example shows is_nested returns 0 or 1 depending on transformed leading ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: NPos_test
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NPos test (I); I monomial ideal. Return: A list whose first element is 1 if I is in Noether position, 0 otherwise. The second element is a list of variables ordered such that those variables are listed first of which a power belongs to the initial ideal of I. If I is in Noether position, method also returns the dimension of I. Assume: I is a nonzero monomial ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From noether.lib. Provides a deterministic test for monomial ideals to check Noether position and variable ordering information. Example referenced with returned separators in earlier sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: modNpos_test
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modNpos test(i); i an ideal. Return: 1 if i is in Noether position 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: This test is probabilistic; computes initial ideal modulo prime 2147483647 (largest prime < 2^31). From noether.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: NPos
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NPos(i); i ideal. Return: A linear map phi such that phi(i) is in Noether position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From noether.lib. Deterministic method to compute transformation putting ideal into Noether position.

rubrics_metrics.name: modNPos
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modNPos(i); i ideal. Return: A linear map phi such that phi(i) is in Noether position. Note: It uses modNpos_test to test Noether position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From noether.lib. Uses probabilistic modular testing to find a linear map that puts ideal into Noether position.

rubrics_metrics.name: nsatiety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: nsatiety (i); i ideal. Return: an integer, the satiety of i. (returns -1 if i is not homogeneous). Assume: i is a homogeneous ideal of the basering R=K[x(0)..x(n)]. Theory: satiety defined as least s such that degree d parts of i and its saturation coincide for all d>=s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From noether.lib. Similar in purpose to satiety in mregular.lib but provided in noether.lib; examples and theory repeated.

rubrics_metrics.name: modsatiety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modsatiety(i); i ideal. Return: an integer, the satiety of i. (returns -1 if i is not homogeneous). Assume: i is a homogeneous ideal of the basering R=K[x(0)..x(n)]. Theory: satiety defined as least s where degree-d parts stabilize with saturation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From noether.lib. Modular/probabilistic variant used to compute satiety; notes parallel nsatiety.
